title: Property of the selected finite upper bound
statement: Let $I$, $d$, $\prec$ and $u$ be as in [def-nagata-directed-finite-upper-bound]. For every finite subset $F\subseteq I$, every $i\in F$ satisfies $i\leq u(F)$.

proof.text: Induct on the number of elements of the finite set $G\subseteq I$, using the fixed auxiliary order $\prec$ from [def-nagata-directed-finite-upper-bound]. For $G=\varnothing$ there is nothing to prove. If $G\neq\varnothing$, let $i$ be the $\prec$-largest element of $G$ and put $F=G\setminus\{i\}$; then $i\notin F$ and $j\prec i$ for every $j\in F$, so by the definition $u(G)=u(F\cup\{i\})=d(u(F),i)$. The selected upper-bound properties of $d$ give $u(F)\le d(u(F),i)$ and $i\le d(u(F),i)$. Every $j\in F$ satisfies $j\le u(F)$ by the induction hypothesis applied to $F$ (which has fewer elements), hence $j\le u(G)$ by transitivity of $\le$; the remaining element $i$ is bounded directly.
